Rashi on Chullin 11b:10:1.hebrew: היכא דאפשר - לעמוד על בירור, בודקין ולא סמכינן ארובא, וצריכין לבדוק בהמה מכל י"ח טרפות. אי נמי, כגון קטן וקטנה דאפשר לנו להמתין עד שיגדלו ונדע שאינו סריס, נמתין. והנך כולהו משום דלא אפשר, הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:10:1.english: Where it is possible - to ascertain the matter with certainty, we examine and do not rely on the majority; and [so] we must examine an animal for all eighteen types of tereifot. Alternatively, [this means] such as a minor boy or minor girl, where it is possible for us to wait until they grow up and we will know that he is not a saris - we wait. But all these other [cases where we do rely on the majority] are because it is not possible [to ascertain the matter directly].

Rashi on Chullin 11b:11:1.hebrew: לרבי מאיר - דלא אזיל בתר רובא, הכי נמי דלא אכל בשרא, משום דשמא במקום נקב קא שחיט:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:11:1.english: According to Rabbi Meir - who does not follow the majority, so too he should not eat meat, because perhaps he slaughtered at the location of a hole.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:1:1.hebrew: ודילמא חד מינייהו - האי דעזאזל טרפה הוא, דבשלמא הך דלשם בדיק ליה לאחר שחיטה, אלא חבירו משתלח לצוק ואין נשחט:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:1:1.english: And perhaps one of them - This one, [the goat] of Azazel, is a tereifah. For granted, the other one, [the goat designated] for the Lord, is checked after its slaughter, but its counterpart is sent off to the cliff and is not slaughtered.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:2:1.hebrew: אין הגורל קובע לעזאזל אלא בראוי לשם - שהרי בשעת הגורל אין ידוע איזה יעלה לשם, הילכך שמעינן ממילא דטרפה לא מייתינן:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:2:1.english: The lottery only designates [a goat] for Azazel when it is fit for the [Divine] Name - For at the time of the lottery it is not known which of them will go up for the [Divine] Name; therefore we learn incidentally that a tereifah is not brought [as a candidate].

Rashi on Chullin 11b:2:2.english: We examine it - After it has been cast off the cliff.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:2:3.hebrew: אברים אברים - ותו לא מצי בדק ליה, דאין יכול לידע איזו שבירה מחיים:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:2:3.english: Limb from limb - [Once the goat is torn apart this way,] he can no longer examine it [to determine whether it was a tereifa], since it is impossible to know which fracture occurred while it was [still] alive.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:4:1.hebrew: בבית האסורין - שם עברתו אמו, ואין לחוש שמא בא עליה אחר, ששניהן לבדם היו עד הוכר העובר:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:4:1.english: In the prison - There his mother conceived him, and there is no need to be concerned that another man came upon her, since the two of them were alone together until the pregnancy became noticeable.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:5:1.hebrew: טרפה הוה - ההרוג, ואין זה ראוי ליהרג, דגברא קטילא קטיל:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:5:1.english: He was a tereifah - [This refers to] the murder victim, and [the murderer] is not liable to be executed for it, since he killed a man who was [already] dead.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:6:1.hebrew: וכי תימא משום איבוד נשמה דהאי - רוצח, דלא לימות, משום דבעינן "ושפטו העדה והצילו העדה" (במדבר לה):
Rashi on Chullin 11b:6:1.english: And if you say [it is] because of the loss of life of this one - [Meaning,] the murderer - that he should not die [before judgment], because we require [the process of] "and the congregation shall judge, and the congregation shall deliver" (Numbers 35).

Rashi on Chullin 11b:6:2.hebrew: נינווליה - להאי נהרג, ואי לאו משתכח טרפה, יהרג רוצח זה:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:6:2.english: His mutilation - [Refers to the mutilation of] this person who was killed. And if [we do] not [examine him], it will not be discovered that he was a tereifah, and this murderer will be executed.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:6:3.hebrew: ואמאי - ליחוש במקום סייף שהרגו בה, נקב היה תחלה, וטרפה הוא, וגברא קטילא קטיל:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:6:3.english: And why [is it not a concern]? - Let us be concerned that at the place of the knife with which he slaughtered it [the animal], there was already a hole beforehand, and it is a tereifah, and he is [in effect] slaughtering an animal that is already dead.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:8:1.hebrew: וכי תימא דבדקינן ליה - כלומר דכשנהרג על ידי עדותן ואח"כ הוזמו, מישתעי קרא, ונבדקיה קודם שנהרגם:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:8:1.english: And if you say that we examine him - That is to say, the verse is speaking of a case where he was killed on the basis of their testimony and they [the witnesses] were only afterward found to be conspiring witnesses - and so [the question is:] let us examine them before they kill him.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:8:2.hebrew: והתניא ברבי אומר - לא ידעינן מנו, אלא אחד גדול בדורו היה, ועל שם כך נקרא ברבי, כדאשכחן בכיצד מעברין בעירובין (דף נג.) אמר רבי אושעיא ברבי, ובפ"ב (לקמן חולין כח.) רבי אלעזר הקפר ברבי:
Rashi on Chullin 11b:8:2.english: And it was taught: "Berabbi says" - We do not know who he is; rather, [we know only that] he was a great man of his generation, and it is for this reason that he is called "Berabbi," as we find in [the chapter] "Keitzad Me'abrin" in Eruvin (page 53a): "Rabbi Oshaya Berabbi said," and in the second chapter (below, Chullin 28a): "Rabbi Elazar HaKappar Berabbi."

Rashi on Chullin 11b:8:3.english: He killed him - [This refers to the time] before they [the witnesses] were proven to be conspiring witnesses [zomemim].

Rashi on Chullin 11b:8:4.english: They are not executed - For it is written, "as he had plotted" (Deuteronomy 19:19), and not "as was actually done."

Rashi on Chullin 11b:9:1.english: It is derived from slaughter itself - Since [the Gemara] has been dealing with it [slaughter] until now.

Rashi on Chullin 11b:9:2.hebrew: דלמא במקום נקב קא שחיט - נקובת הושט במשהו, אבל גרגרת ברובא, ואם חסרה בכאיסר טרפה, באלו טרפות (לקמן חולין דף מה.):
Rashi on Chullin 11b:9:2.english: Perhaps he is slaughtering at the place of the hole - A perforation of the esophagus [renders the animal] tereifah with even a minuscule amount, but the windpipe [is tereifah only if perforated] through the majority [of its circumference]; and if it is missing [flesh] the size of an issar, it is tereifah - [as taught] in [the chapter] Eilu Tereifot (below, Chullin 45a).

Tosafot on Chullin 11b:11:1.hebrew:
לרבי מאיר דחייש למיעוטא כו' - מדקאמר "לרבי מאיר" ולא קאמר "היכי אכלינן", משמע דלא קיימא לן כר' מאיר דחייש למיעוטא. וקשה, דבפרק הלוקח בהמה (בכורות כד.) פסיק רבי יוחנן כרשב"ג, דאמר הלוקח בהמה מניקה מן העובד כוכבים דפטורה מן הבכורה כשבנה כרוך אחריה, משום דלא מרחמא ליה אא"כ ילדה, אבל מטעם חלב לא מיפטר, אע"ג דרוב בהמות אינן חולבות אא"כ יולדות; אלמא חיישינן למיעוטא, אע"ג דליכא חזקה בהדי מיעוטא, דאי אמרינן אוקי בהמה בחזקת שלא ילדה, אדרבה העמד וולד בחזקת שאינו קדוש בבכורה, שהיה חולין במעי אמו. ויש לומר דרבי יוחנן לא פסיק כוותיה אלא בהא דלא מרחמא אלא אם כן ילדה:
ונפקא מינה להיכי שראינוה שהיה לה חלב קודם לידה, דההיא לא מפטרינן מטעם חלב, ואפשר דאף רשב"ג סבר דחלב פוטר. והשתא אתי שפיר, דאשכחן רשב"ג דלא חייש למיעוטא בריש כל הצלמים (ע"ז דף מ:), דלא גזר שאר מקומות אטו אותו מקום, כדגזר ר"מ התם. ורבי יוחנן נמי אכל לעיל (חולין דף ה:) משחיטת כותי, ולא גזר בהו כדגזר ר"מ. ובעשרה יוחסין (קידושין דף פ.) גבי שני דברים שאין בהן דעת לישאל ועשאן הכתוב כו', משמע נמי דרבי יוחנן כרבנן דר"מ ס"ל. והא דא"ר יוחנן בסוף אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף לט:) למעוטי מורייס וגבינות בית אונייקי, וסתמא כר"מ - התם הוי סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת בריש כל הצלמים (עבודה זרה מ:). והא דאמר רשב"ג כל ששהה שלשים יום באדם אינו נפל, הא לא שהה ספק הוי, אפילו נפל מן הגג או אכלו ארי, בפרק ר' אליעזר דמילה (שבת דף קלה:), וקיימא לן התם כוותיה אע"ג דרובן אינן נפלים; וכן תוך שמנה ימים בבהמה אסרינן התם ולא אזלינן בתר רובא. התם משום דלא יבא להקל בערוה, והצריכוה חליצה במת תוך שלשים, ולא רצו לסמוך על הרוב ולהתירה לשוק בלא חליצה, שלא יאמרו העולם שפיהק ומת, ויבא לידי לעז וקלקול; ולכך גם לענין אבילות פטור, שלא יבא להקל בערוה. ועוד, דבלאו הכי יש להקל באבילות, דקי"ל (מו"ק דף [יח.] כ.) הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל. ואסרו כמו כן בבהמה, דגזרו בהמה אטו אדם, דאי לא הא לא קיימא הא; אי נמי, אסור בבהמה אפי' בבריא, שלא יבא להתירה בחולה שיהא קרוב לפיהק ומת:
Tosafot on Chullin 11b:11:1.english: According to Rabbi Meir, who is concerned for the minority, etc. - From the fact that [the Gemara] said "according to Rabbi Meir" and did not say "how do we eat [the meat]?", it implies that we do not hold like Rabbi Meir, who is concerned for the minority. But this is difficult, for in the chapter "One Who Buys an Animal" (Bechorot 24a), Rabbi Yochanan ruled in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said that one who buys a nursing animal from a non-Jew is exempt from [the sanctity of] the firstborn when her calf follows after her, because she does not show it affection unless she gave birth to it - but she is not exempted on account of the reasoning about milk, even though most animals do not give milk unless they have given birth. This shows that we are concerned for the minority, even though there is no supporting chazakah (presumption) alongside the minority - for if we say, "place the animal in its presumptive status of not having given birth," on the contrary, place the offspring in its presumptive status of not being sanctified as a firstborn, since it was non-sacred while in its mother's womb. And one can say that Rabbi Yochanan ruled like him [Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel] only regarding the point that she does not show affection unless she gave birth. And the practical difference [between the two reasons] is in a case where we saw that she had milk before giving birth - that case is not exempted on account of the milk reasoning, and it is possible that even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that milk exempts [only when linked to an actual birth]. And now this works out well, for we find that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is not concerned for the minority at the beginning of "Kol HaTzelamim" (Avodah Zarah 40b), where he did not extend the decree to the other parts [of the city] on account of that one place, as Rabbi Meir decreed there. And Rabbi Yochanan too, above (Chullin 5b), ate from the slaughtering of a Samaritan (Kuthi), and did not decree against them as Rabbi Meir decreed. And in [the chapter] "Asarah Yuchasin" (Kiddushin 80a), regarding the two matters that have no capacity to be asked [about their intent], "and Scripture made them," etc., it likewise implies that Rabbi Yochanan holds like the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Meir. And as for what Rabbi Yochanan said at the end of [the chapter] "Ein Ma'amidin" (Avodah Zarah 39b), to exclude fish-brine and the cheeses of Beit Unyaki [from a stringency] - and the anonymous [teaching] there follows Rabbi Meir - there, it was [first taught] anonymously, and afterward there is a dispute at the beginning of "Kol HaTzelamim" (Avodah Zarah 40b) [so no proof can be drawn from it]. And as for what Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said, that any [infant] who survived thirty days is not deemed a nefel (non-viable) - implying that if he did not survive, it is a doubt, even if he fell from the roof or a lion ate him - this is stated in the chapter "Rabbi Eliezer of Milah" (Shabbat 135b), and we hold like him there, even though most [such infants] are not nefalim. And likewise, within eight days in the case of an animal [regarding firstborn status], we rule stringently there and do not follow the majority. There, [the reason is] so that one should not come to be lenient in a matter of forbidden relations (ervah): they required chalitzah for the widow whose [infant] died within thirty days, and they did not want to rely on the majority and permit her to remarry without chalitzah, lest people say "he merely yawned and died," which would lead to slander and impropriety. And therefore, with regard to mourning as well, one is exempt [from mourning such an infant], so as not to come to be lenient in a matter of forbidden relations. And furthermore, aside from this, there is reason to be lenient regarding mourning, since we hold (Mo'ed Katan 18a/20a) that the halachah follows the lenient view in [laws of] mourning. And they likewise forbade [relying on the majority] regarding an animal, since they decreed that the animal [case] follows the human [case] - for were it not so, the other [decree] would not stand; alternatively, [the offspring] is treated stringently in the case of an animal even when it is healthy, so that one should not come to permit it in the case of a sick [animal], which is close to "dying suddenly."

Tosafot on Chullin 11b:4:1.hebrew: כגון שהיו אביו ואמו חבושים בבית האסורין - ועוד הוה מצי למידק, ודילמא משום דאזלינן בתר חזקה דהעמד האם בחזקת צדקת:
Tosafot on Chullin 11b:4:1.english: For example, where his father and mother were imprisoned - Additionally, one could have raised a further difficulty: but perhaps [there is no need for this specific case of seclusion, since] we follow the presumption (chazakah) that establishes the mother's status as one of chastity.

Tosafot on Chullin 11b:6:1.hebrew: וכי תימא דבדקינן ליה - מקשינן דנילף מרוצח גופיה דאזלינן בתר רובא, דדילמא הרוצח הוא טרפה, וטרפה שהרג את הנפש פטור. ושמא דאזלינן בתר רובא מדלא חיישינן להרוג את הטרפה, לא נילף בעלמא. ועוד נראה לי דטעמא דטרפה שהרג פטור, דהיינו משום דהוי עדות שאין אתה יכול להזימה, ואי קטלינן עדים כשהוזמו לא שפיר קטלינן. ואם כן, אין להוכיח אלא במאי דקטלינן לעדים, ולא חיישינן דלמא הך דאסהידו ביה טרפה הוה, כדקאמר בסמוך. וכן מצינו בשם רבינו מנחם הקדוש. אך קשה לי, מאי קאמר וכי תימא דבדקינן ליה, הא מכל מקום הויא ליה התראת ספק, אי לא אזלינן בתר רובא. ושמא קסבר דשמה התראה:
Tosafot on Chullin 11b:6:1.english: And if you would say that we check him - We raise a difficulty: [why not] learn [this] from the murderer himself, regarding whom we follow the majority - for perhaps the murderer is a tereifah [one with a fatal wound], and a tereifah who killed a person is exempt [from execution, yet we still rely on the majority and execute him]. And perhaps [the reason] we follow the majority there is that we are not concerned lest we thereby execute a tereifah - but we cannot derive [a general rule] from it elsewhere. And it further seems to me that the reason a tereifah who killed [a person] is exempt is that it is testimony against which you cannot [validly] apply hazamah (the "zomemin" procedure); for if we would execute the witnesses once they are proven zomemin [in such a case], we would not be executing them properly. And if so, [the law] can only be proven from a case where we [validly] execute the witnesses, and we need not worry that perhaps the one about whom they testified was a tereifah, as it says shortly. And so, too, we find in the name of Rabbeinu Menachem HaKadosh. But this is difficult for me: what is meant by "and if you would say that we check him"? In any event he would have only a doubtful warning (hatra'at safek), if we do not follow the majority. And perhaps he holds that a doubtful warning is nonetheless considered a valid warning.

Tosafot on Chullin 11b:6:2.hebrew: ליחוש דלמא במקום סייף נקב הוה - אין להקשות משכחת לה כגון שהטביעו בנהר דאפשר בתר הכי למיבדקיה, דהא קרא בכלי עץ ובכלי ברזל ואבן כתיב. אבל קשה דמשכחת לה כגון שהיה קרום של מוח מגולה וראו שהיה שלם, ובא זה ונקבו והרגו. ויש לומר דדוחק הוא להעמיד הפסוק בכך. ואם תאמר: ובספ"ק דמכות (דף ז.) דאמרי רבי טרפון ורבי עקיבא: אילו היינו בסנהדרין לא היה אדם נהרג, ומפרש דהוו בדקו להו ואמרי: ראיתם שטריפה הרג או שלם הרג? ואם תמצא לומר שלם הרג, שמא במקום סייף נקב הוה; והכא משמע דלא חיישינן, דאזלינן בתר רובא. ויש לומר דרבי עקיבא לטעמיה, דאמר דחיישינן למיעוטא בפרק הלוקח בהמה (בכורות כ:), דקסבר חלב אינו פוטר בבהמה בבכורה, אע"ג דרוב בהמות אינן חולבות אא"כ יולדות; ואע"ג דאפילו רבי מאיר דחייש למיעוטא מודה היכא דלא אפשר, רבי עקיבא חשיב ליה אפשר, דאיכא לאוקמי קרא שהיה קרום מוחו מגולה ונקבו כדפירשנו. ורשב"ג דפליג עלייהו ואמר: אף הם מרבים שופכי דמים בישראל, אפילו חייש למיעוטא, מ"מ חשיב ליה לא אפשר, דדוחק הוא להעמיד הפסוק בכך. ועוד אור"ת, דאף על גב דאי לא שיילינן לעדים קטלינן ליה דסמכינן ארובא, היכא דלא אפשר; היכא דשיילינן להו ואמרי דלא ידעי, פטור - מידי דהוה אסייף וארירן, דאי לא שיילינן להו חייב, ואי שיילינן להו ואמר אחד בסייף ואחד בארירן פטור. אע"ג דבסייף וארירן כשאומרים אין אנו יודעין חייב עד דמכחשי אהדדי, היינו משום דסייף וארירן לא שייך כל כך בגוף העדות, דמה לי הרגו בסייף ומה לי בארירן; אבל במקום סייף נקב הוה, דשייך לגוף העדות טפי, אי בדקינן להו ואמרו אין אנו יודעין - פטור. ואחד אומר כליו שחורים ואחד אומר כליו לבנים, דלא שייך לגוף העדות, אע"פ דמכחשי אהדדי - חייב. הקשה רבינו יצחק ברבי מרדכי, דהכא ילפינן מרוצח ועדים זוממים דאזלינן בתר רובא אף בדיני נפשות, וכן מוכח בריש פ' בן סורר ומורה (סנהדרין דף סט.) ובאלו הן הנשרפין (שם דף עט:), אמרינן: נסקלין בנשרפין ידונו בסקילה הקלה, אע"ג דרוב נשרפים נינהו. ותירץ ר"ת, דכיון דממה נפשך הוא נהרג, לענין באיזו מיתה הוא נהרג לא אזלינן בתר רובא. ועוד יש לומר דהוי קבוע וכמחצה על מחצה דמי. והא דפריך התם מעיקרא: כי הוה תני הנשרפין בנסקלין, תיפוק ליה דרובא נסקלין נינהו - הכי פירושו: לכל הפחות לא גרע משום דהוו רובא דנסקלין:
Tosafot on Chullin 11b:6:2.english: Let us be concerned lest the perforation was precisely where the sword struck - One should not object that you can find a [parallel] case, such as where they drowned him in a river - for it is possible to examine him afterward [and there this concern would not apply] - since the verse is written [only] with regard to a wooden implement, an iron implement, and a stone. But it is difficult, for you can find a case such as where the membrane covering the brain was exposed, and they saw that it was intact, and this one came and perforated it and killed him [and there the same concern would apply even though examination was possible]. And one can answer that it is a forced [reading] to establish the verse in that way. And if you say: at the end of the first chapter of Makkot (7a), where Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva say, "Had we been in the Sanhedrin, no person would ever have been executed," and it is explained that they would examine [the witnesses] and say, "Did you see that he killed a tereifah, or that he killed a whole [healthy person]?" - and even if you would say that he killed a whole person, [one could still object:] perhaps the perforation was precisely where the sword struck - and here [in our sugya] it implies that we are not concerned about this, since we follow the majority. One can answer that Rabbi Akiva follows his own reasoning, for he holds elsewhere that we are concerned for the minority - in the chapter "One Who Buys an Animal" (Bechorot 20b), where he holds that [the presence of] milk does not exempt an animal from firstborn status, even though the majority of animals do not produce milk unless they have given birth. And even though even Rabbi Meir, who is [generally] concerned for the minority, concedes that one follows the majority where it is not possible [to explain otherwise], Rabbi Akiva considers it possible here, since one can establish the verse [as referring to] a case where the membrane of his brain was exposed and they perforated it, as we explained. And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who disagrees with them and says, "They too increase the shedders of blood in Israel" - even though he too is [generally] concerned for the minority, he nevertheless considers this a case where [that reading] is "not possible," since it is a forced [reading] to establish the verse in that way. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam said: although if we do not question the witnesses [about the victim's condition] we execute [the accused], relying on the majority - that is only where it is not possible to question them. Where we do question them and they say that they do not know, he is exempt - just as is the case with a sword and an ariran [another weapon]: if we do not question them [about which weapon was used], he is liable; but if we do question them, and one witness says [it was] by sword and one says by an ariran, he is exempt. And [although] with sword and ariran, when both witnesses say "we do not know," he remains liable - [testimony becoming void] only once they [directly] contradict one another - this is because [the difference between] a sword and an ariran is not so intrinsic to the substance of the testimony, for what difference does it make to me whether he killed him with a sword or with an ariran? But [when the claim is] "perhaps the perforation was precisely where the sword struck," which is more intrinsic to the substance of the testimony, if we examine them and they say "we do not know," he is exempt. Whereas if one witness says his garments were black and one says his garments were white - since that is not intrinsic to the substance of the testimony - even though they contradict one another, he is liable. Rabbeinu Yitzchak son of Rabbi Mordechai raised a difficulty: for here we derive from [the cases of] a murderer and conspiring witnesses that we follow the majority even in capital cases, and so it is proven at the beginning of the chapter "Ben Sorer u-Moreh" (Sanhedrin 69a) and in [the chapter] "Eilu Hein HaNisrafin" (ibid. 79b), where we say: "[Those liable to] stoning [mixed] among [those liable to] burning are judged with the lighter [penalty], stoning" - even though the majority are [liable to] burning. And Rabbeinu Tam answered that since, either way, he is executed, we do not follow the majority with regard to by which method of execution he is executed. And furthermore, one can say that this is a case of something "fixed" (kavua), which is treated as an even mixture. And as for the Gemara's initial question there - "When it taught [the law of] those [liable to] burning [judged] among those [liable to] stoning, let this be derived simply because the majority are those [liable to] stoning" - this is what it means: at the very least, [the ruling] is not weakened by the fact that they are also a majority of those [liable to] stoning.

Tosafot on Chullin 11b:7:1.hebrew: ודילמא הך דאסהידו ביה טרפה הוה - ואם תאמר דחובשים אותו י"ב חדש, ואם יחיה לאו טרפה הוא, ויש לומר דשמא קסבר טרפה חיה. ועוד נראה לי, דאי אין הורגין העדים כשהוזמו אלא אחר י"ב חדש, דדילמא הך דאסהידו ביה טרפה, א"כ גם אותו שמעידין עליו אין להורגו עד לאחר י"ב חדש; וכיון דלא באו להורגו אלא אחר י"ב חדש, א"כ לא יהרגו הם אף לאחר י"ב חדש, דדילמא נעשה טרפה הך דאסהידו ביה בסוף י"ב חדשים, והרי לא באו אלא להרוג את הטריפה:
Tosafot on Chullin 11b:7:1.english: But perhaps the one about whom they testified was a tereifah! - And if you say: they imprison him twelve months, and if he lives, he is not a tereifah; one can answer that perhaps he holds that a tereifah [can] live. And it further seems to me that if the witnesses are not executed, once they are found to be zomemin, except after twelve months — because perhaps the one about whom they testified was a tereifah — if so, the one against whom they testify [likewise] should not be executed until after twelve months; and since they came to have him executed only after twelve months, then they [the witnesses] should not be executed even after twelve months either, for perhaps the one about whom they testified became a tereifah at the end of the twelve months — and, in that case, they had come only to kill [one who turned out to be] a tereifah.
